      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "proteins",
      "verbatim": "A blasting effort between mouse, rat, and human using the PhosphoSitePlus (PSP) sites in each species and a strict match criterion suggests that 96.2%–99.6% of the proteins blasted share more than 75% of their total aa sequences, indicating a high accuracy of blast function applied to phosphoproteomics (Figures S1 D–S1G)."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "P-sites mapped",
      "value": 87716,
      "unit": "count",
      "measures": "experimentally identified P-sites in human that were successfully mapped to corresponding sites in mouse sequence",
      "compared": "human P-sites to mouse sequence",
      "species": [
        "human",
        "mouse"
      ],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "P-sites",
      "verbatim": "We found that using simple aa similarity scores ≥8, a total of 87,716 P-sites experimentally identified in human were successfully mapped to the corresponding sites in the mouse sequence."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "P-sites confidently identified in mouse",
      "value": 23040,
      "unit": "count",
      "measures": "experimentally identified human P-sites that were confidently identified in mouse phosphoproteomic analysis",
      "compared": "human P-sites to mouse identified P-sites",
      "species": [
        "human",
        "mouse"
      ],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "P-sites",
      "verbatim": "Intriguingly, out of these P-sites, 23,040 (62.35% of the assembled mouse dataset) were confidently identified by the comprehensive MS analysis in the mouse. 21 (Figure 2 C)."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "Kinase-substrate (KS) annotation increase",
      "value": 3.37,
      "unit": "fold",
      "measures": "increase in kinase-substrate information provided after PTMoreR processing",
      "compared": "original identified phosphopeptides vs. blasted results for KS annotation",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": "kinase-substrate information",
      "verbatim": "Moreover, about 81% of those kinases and substrates from the originally identified phosphopeptides (790/978) were still covered, whereas 3.37 times more KS information (i.e., 2,666) was provided in the blasted results."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "P-sites mapped to Human.identified",
      "value": 29000,
      "unit": "count",
      "measures": "predicted P-sites in 128 mammalian species mapped to the experimentally derived human phosphoproteome",
      "compared": "predicted P-sites in 128 mammalian species to human phosphoproteome",
      "species": [
        "human"
      ],
      "n": 128,
      "n_counts": "mammalian species",
      "verbatim": "Next, we applied PTMoreR in a “reversed” manner (i.e., from human to other mammals) to predict the expressed and potentially detectable P-sites in each of the 128 species, resulting in 29,000–95,000 P-sites mapped to the experimentally derived human phosphoproteome (Human.identified)."
    },
    {

      "verbatim": "We found that S<>S (73.08%), T<>T (19.14%), and Y<>Y (5.65%) ranked in the top three, followed by S<>T (2.01%), and S/T<>Y (0.15%)."

  "headline_index": 0,
  "what_the_study_did": "The study developed and validated a tool called PTMoreR for cross-species PTM mapping and comparative phosphoproteomics.",
